quests.instruction: Identify the pitch pattern. What does the speaker mean by this pitch? A host expects you to pick one drink.
quests.word: Would you like tea or coffee?
quests.textToSpeak: Would you like tea or coffee?
options: Rises on both: asking whether you want any drink
Rises on tea, falls on coffee: choose one of the two
quests.correctAnswer: Rises on tea, falls on coffee: choose one of the two
quests.hint: Listen to what happens on each option, and especially on the last one.
quests.explanation: The rise on TEA says 'there is another option coming', and the fall on COFFEE closes the choice. Rising on both would turn it into a yes/no offer.
quests.emphasisRule: In an alternative question, every option but the last rises and the last one falls.

quests.instruction: Identify the emphasis. A traveller must choose how to reach the city.
quests.word: Are you taking the bus or the train?
quests.textToSpeak: Are you taking the bus or the train?
options: Emphasis on BUS and TRAIN
Emphasis on TAKING and BUS
quests.correctAnswer: Emphasis on BUS and TRAIN
quests.hint: The verb is the same for both choices. Which words differ?
quests.explanation: TAKING is shared by both options, so it stays low. BUS and TRAIN are the alternatives, so each gets a peak, with the voice falling on the last one.
quests.emphasisRule: In an alternative question, the contrasting options carry the peaks and the shared verb stays low.

quests.instruction: Identify the pitch pattern. What does the speaker mean by this pitch? A host asks whether you want a drink; tea and coffee are just examples.
quests.word: Can I get you tea or coffee or something?
quests.textToSpeak: Can I get you tea or coffee or something?
options: Falls at the end: asking you to pick one of tea or coffee, nothing else
Rises at the end: offering a drink, with tea and coffee as examples
quests.correctAnswer: Rises at the end: offering a drink, with tea and coffee as examples
quests.hint: 'Or something' changes the shape of the offer. What does it do to the choice?
quests.explanation: The final rise on 'something' leaves the offer open, so tea and coffee are only suggestions. A fall at the end would turn it back into a pick-one question.
quests.emphasisRule: A rise that continues past the last option makes a choice open-ended.

quests.instruction: Identify the pitch pattern. What does the speaker mean by this pitch? A café worker asks for your size.
options: Rises on small and medium, falls on large: pick one of three
Rises on all three: asking if you want any size
quests.correctAnswer: Rises on small and medium, falls on large: pick one of three
quests.hint: Think about what each rise leaves open, and how the last item closes things.
quests.explanation: SMALL and MEDIUM each lift because more options follow, and LARGE falls because the choice is complete. A rise on LARGE would ask whether any size is wanted.
quests.emphasisRule: In a closed choice of three or more, every option rises except the last.

quests.instruction: Identify the emphasis. You and a friend have ruled out taking a taxi to the airport.
quests.word: So, are we taking the bus, the metro, or driving?
quests.textToSpeak: So, are we taking the bus, the metro, or driving?
options: Emphasis on BUS, METRO, and DRIVING
Emphasis on TAKING, METRO, and DRIVING
quests.correctAnswer: Emphasis on BUS, METRO, and DRIVING
quests.hint: The taxi is already out. How many peaks should you hear in the choice itself?
quests.explanation: TAKING is the shared verb for the first two options and stays low. Each remaining option gets a peak, BUS first and METRO next, with the last one, DRIVING, falling to close the choice.
quests.emphasisRule: Each option in a list of choices carries its own peak; the shared frame stays low.

quests.instruction: Identify the pitch pattern. What does the speaker mean by this pitch? A waiter mentions a few desserts, but there are more.
quests.word: We have cake, pie, ice cream...
quests.textToSpeak: We have cake, pie, ice cream...
options: Rises on every item, including the last: the list continues
Falls on the last item: the list is complete and nothing else follows
quests.correctAnswer: Rises on every item, including the last: the list continues
quests.hint: The waiter hasn't finished. What does the voice do on the last item?
quests.explanation: The rise on ICE CREAM keeps the list open, which is how a waiter signals 'and more'. A fall would close the menu.
quests.emphasisRule: A rise on the last item of a list leaves it open.

quests.instruction: Identify the pitch pattern. What does the speaker mean by this pitch? You're sure the deadline is tomorrow and want agreement.
options: Falling tag: you already know and expect agreement
Rising tag: you really aren't sure and need to be told
quests.correctAnswer: Falling tag: you already know and expect agreement
quests.hint: How confident is the speaker? Listen to what the tag does.
quests.explanation: A falling 'isn't it' says 'I know this, please agree'. A rising tag would reveal real doubt.
quests.emphasisRule: A falling tag seeks agreement; a rising tag seeks information.

quests.instruction: Identify the pitch pattern. What does the speaker mean by this pitch? You can't remember whether the shop closes at six.
quests.word: The shop closes at six, doesn't it?
quests.textToSpeak: The shop closes at six, doesn't it?
options: Rising tag: a real question
Falling tag: expecting agreement
quests.correctAnswer: Rising tag: a real question
quests.hint: This time the speaker genuinely doesn't know. How does the tag end?
quests.explanation: The rise on 'doesn't it' asks for information because the speaker is unsure. A falling tag would sound as if the speaker already knew.
quests.emphasisRule: A rising tag signals real uncertainty.

quests.instruction: Identify the pitch pattern. What does the speaker mean by this pitch? Two tourists admire the view from a hill.
quests.word: It's a great place, isn't it?
quests.textToSpeak: It's a great place, isn't it?
options: Falling tag: sharing an opinion and inviting agreement
Rising tag: asking for information about the place
quests.correctAnswer: Falling tag: sharing an opinion and inviting agreement
quests.hint: No facts are being asked for. What is the speaker doing?
quests.explanation: An opinion isn't something the listener can look up, so the falling tag just invites them to share the feeling.
quests.emphasisRule: A falling tag on an opinion invites shared feeling, not information.

quests.instruction: Identify the pitch pattern. What does the speaker mean by this pitch? A caller says her appointment is "Tuesday at three." You repeat it to confirm.
options: Falling: telling the caller what the time is
Rising: checking the detail you heard, not stating it
quests.correctAnswer: Rising: checking the detail you heard, not stating it
quests.hint: You are not giving new information. What is the repeated phrase for?
quests.explanation: Repeating a detail with a rise checks that you heard it correctly. A fall would sound as though you were stating it yourself.
quests.emphasisRule: A repeated detail with a rising ending asks the speaker to confirm.

quests.instruction: Identify the emphasis. A coach says practice has moved to a field. You're sure about 'field' but not which one.
options: Emphasis on FIELD
Emphasis on NORTH
quests.correctAnswer: Emphasis on NORTH
quests.hint: You only doubt one word. Which word is it?
quests.explanation: FIELD is understood, so it carries only the rise. NORTH is the part you're checking, so it takes the early peak.
quests.emphasisRule: When confirming by repeating, the doubtful word takes the peak.

quests.instruction: Identify the pitch pattern. What does the speaker mean by this pitch? A hotel clerk is confirming your booking details.
quests.word: So that's two nights, starting Friday?
quests.textToSpeak: So that's two nights, starting Friday?
options: Falling: announcing it as settled
Rising: checking the whole summary
quests.correctAnswer: Rising: checking the whole summary
quests.hint: The clerk wants you to agree before continuing. What does the ending do?
quests.explanation: The rise on FRIDAY invites you to confirm the whole summary. A fall would close the topic before you had a chance to correct anything.
quests.emphasisRule: A summary with a rising ending asks for confirmation.

quests.instruction: Identify the emphasis. Your friend mumbles that she lost something on the train, and you didn't catch what.
options: Emphasis on LOST
Emphasis on WHAT
quests.correctAnswer: Emphasis on WHAT
quests.hint: You caught part of the sentence. Which piece did you fail to hear?
quests.explanation: LOST is understood, so it falls away. WHAT replaces the part you missed and takes the peak with the rise.
quests.emphasisRule: In an echo question, the question word replaces the missing part and takes the peak.

quests.instruction: Identify the emphasis. A says: "We paid fifty thousand for the kitchen." B reacts:
quests.word: You paid how much for it?
quests.textToSpeak: You paid how much for it?
options: Emphasis on MUCH
Emphasis on PAID
quests.correctAnswer: Emphasis on MUCH
quests.hint: B heard the amount but can't believe it. What is B questioning?
quests.explanation: PAID is repeated, so it stays low. MUCH is the part B is reacting to, so the peak lands on it. IT is a weak pronoun at the end.
quests.emphasisRule: In an echo question, the questioned word takes the peak and a final pronoun stays weak.

quests.instruction: Identify the pitch pattern. What does the speaker mean by this pitch? A says: "I quit my job on Monday." B reacts:
options: Echoing the verb to express surprise
Asking a new question about the job
quests.correctAnswer: Echoing the verb to express surprise
quests.hint: A has just given news. Is B asking for new information, or reacting to what was said?
quests.explanation: B repeats QUIT, the surprising word from A's news. This is an echo of surprise, not a request for new details.
quests.emphasisRule: An echo of the key word with a rise expresses surprise.

quests.instruction: Identify the pitch pattern. What does the speaker mean by this pitch? A says: "Send the invoice to Ms. Vasquez." B didn't catch the name.
options: Echoing the part you didn't catch
Asking a yes/no question about the invoice
quests.correctAnswer: Echoing the part you didn't catch
quests.hint: B isn't asking about the invoice. Which part of A's sentence is B responding to?
quests.explanation: B repeats the title and replaces the missing name with WHO, rising to show it needs repeating. It is a clarification, not a new question.
quests.emphasisRule: A partial echo with a question word asks the speaker to repeat the missing part.

quests.instruction: Identify the pitch pattern. What does the speaker mean by this pitch? A speaker mumbles a number and B can't tell which one.
quests.word: Did you say twelve or twenty?
quests.textToSpeak: Did you say twelve or twenty?
options: Rises on twelve, falls on twenty: choosing between two
Falls on both: stating two separate numbers
quests.correctAnswer: Rises on twelve, falls on twenty: choosing between two
quests.hint: The two numbers sound alike. How does the voice present them?
quests.explanation: The rise on TWELVE and the fall on TWENTY give the pattern of an alternative question, so B is asking A to pick one of the two.
quests.emphasisRule: A clarifying choice uses the alternative-question pattern: rise, then fall.

quests.instruction: Identify the emphasis. A says: "The new policy starts in the third quarter." B wants to narrow it down.
quests.word: The third quarter of this year?
quests.textToSpeak: The third quarter of this year?
options: Emphasis on QUARTER
Emphasis on THIS
quests.correctAnswer: Emphasis on THIS
quests.hint: B understood the quarter. What is the remaining doubt?
quests.explanation: QUARTER and THIRD are already settled, so they stay low. THIS is the part B isn't sure about, so it takes the peak.
quests.emphasisRule: In a clarifying echo, the part being clarified takes the peak.

quests.instruction: Identify the emphasis. A asks: "Are you taking the bus or the train?" B answers:
options: Emphasis on I'M and DRIVING
Emphasis on NEITHER and DRIVING
quests.correctAnswer: Emphasis on NEITHER and DRIVING
quests.hint: B rejects both options. Which words show that?
quests.explanation: NEITHER rejects both of A's options, so it gets a peak at the start. DRIVING is the new option and takes the second peak. I'M is just a link.
quests.emphasisRule: A reply that rejects both choices peaks on 'neither' and on the new option.

quests.instruction: Identify the emphasis. A asks: "Do you want the red or the blue?" B wants both.
options: Emphasis on BOTH
Emphasis on TAKE
quests.correctAnswer: Emphasis on BOTH
quests.hint: 'Of them' is a quick pronoun phrase. What does B emphasise instead?
quests.explanation: THEM is a weak pronoun, so the peak moves earlier to BOTH, the word that answers A's either-or question.
quests.emphasisRule: The word answering the choice takes the peak; a final pronoun phrase stays low.

quests.instruction: Identify the pitch pattern. What does the speaker mean by this pitch? A asks: "Tea or coffee?" B hesitates.
options: Falling on tea: a firm choice
Rising on tea: not fully sure of the choice
quests.correctAnswer: Rising on tea: not fully sure of the choice
quests.hint: The speaker adds 'I think'. What does that do to the sound of 'tea'?
quests.explanation: The voice lifts on TEA instead of settling, which matches the hedge 'I think'. A firm choice would fall.
quests.emphasisRule: A rise or fall-rise on the chosen item signals that the choice is tentative.

quests.instruction: Identify the emphasis. Your neighbour is carrying a box and a lamp. She can manage the box.
options: Emphasis on TAKE
Emphasis on LAMP
quests.correctAnswer: Emphasis on LAMP
quests.hint: The offer is about one of two things. Which one?
quests.explanation: She can manage the box, so the offer is only for the lamp. LAMP takes the peak, and the rise makes it an offer.
quests.emphasisRule: In an offer between two objects, the object being offered takes the peak.

quests.instruction: Identify the emphasis. A says: "I'm making tea. Anyone else?" B accepts warmly.
options: Emphasis on LOVE
Emphasis on SOME
quests.correctAnswer: Emphasis on LOVE
quests.hint: 'Some' is a weak word. Which word carries the warmth?
quests.explanation: SOME is a quick pronoun, so it can't hold the peak. LOVE carries the enthusiasm of the acceptance.
quests.emphasisRule: In an enthusiastic reply, the feeling word takes the peak and a final pronoun stays weak.

quests.instruction: Identify the emphasis. A host offers a second helping of dessert. You politely decline.
options: Emphasis on POSSIBLY
Emphasis on COULDN'T
quests.correctAnswer: Emphasis on POSSIBLY
quests.hint: The refusal is softened by an adverb. Which word carries the polite 'no'?
quests.explanation: POSSIBLY is what makes the refusal sound polite and final, so it gets the main lift. COULDN'T is only the frame.
quests.emphasisRule: In polite refusals, the softening adverb carries the peak.

quests.instruction: Identify the pitch pattern. What does the speaker mean by this pitch? A hotel clerk reads back your phone number to confirm it.
options: Rises on each group, then falls: closing the number as confirmed
Rises on each group, with a final rise: asking for confirmation
quests.correctAnswer: Rises on each group, with a final rise: asking for confirmation
quests.hint: Each group of digits promises more. What does the last group do?
quests.explanation: A rise on the last group asks you to confirm the whole number. A fall would announce it as settled and leave no room to correct it.
quests.emphasisRule: A final rise on the last digit group asks the listener to confirm.

quests.instruction: Identify the emphasis. A courier checks the house number but is sure about the street.
options: Emphasis on TWELVE
Emphasis on MILL
quests.correctAnswer: Emphasis on TWELVE
quests.hint: He is certain of one part. Which part is he checking?
quests.explanation: He knows the street, so MILL stays low. TWELVE is the number he wants confirmed, and it carries the peak.
quests.emphasisRule: When checking part of an address, the unsure part takes the peak.

quests.instruction: Identify the pitch pattern. What does the speaker mean by this pitch? A customer service agent finishes checking your details.
quests.word: And that's the same email address as before?
quests.textToSpeak: And that's the same email address as before?
options: Rising: asking whether it's still correct
Falling: telling you that it is still correct
quests.correctAnswer: Rising: asking whether it's still correct
quests.hint: The agent can't know without you. What does her voice do?
quests.explanation: The rise at the end hands the question to you, because only you know if the address has changed.
quests.emphasisRule: A final rise on a confirmation question asks the other person to verify.

quests.instruction: Identify the pitch pattern. What does the speaker mean by this pitch? You can't remember who called.
quests.word: It was Jamal who called, wasn't it?
quests.textToSpeak: It was Jamal who called, wasn't it?
options: Rising: you honestly can't remember
Falling: you're confident and expect agreement
quests.correctAnswer: Rising: you honestly can't remember
quests.hint: The context tells you the speaker is unsure. What does the tag do?
quests.explanation: A rising tag matches the speaker's doubt: it genuinely asks for confirmation. A falling tag would sound as if the speaker already knew.
quests.emphasisRule: A rising tag signals real doubt.

quests.instruction: Identify the emphasis. A says: "Dad's putting the house on the market." B reacts:
options: Emphasis on HE'S
Emphasis on SELLING
quests.correctAnswer: Emphasis on SELLING
quests.hint: B is repeating what A implied. Which part is B reacting to?
quests.explanation: HE'S is given, and IT is a weak pronoun. SELLING is what B is shocked about, so it takes the peak.
quests.emphasisRule: An echo of an implied action takes the peak on the verb; the pronouns stay weak.

quests.instruction: Identify the pitch pattern. What does the speaker mean by this pitch? You phone to confirm a hair appointment and read back the day.
options: Falling on 'right': closing the call
Rising on 'right': asking for a final confirmation
quests.correctAnswer: Rising on 'right': asking for a final confirmation
quests.hint: The speaker needs the salon to agree before hanging up. What does the final word do?
quests.explanation: The rise on RIGHT turns the summary into a request for confirmation. A fall would end the exchange without waiting for a reply.
quests.emphasisRule: A short tag with a rise asks for the final check.
